plan: Store the input dictionary as a private deep copy at construction so external mutation cannot affect the workspace, and have to_data() return a fresh deep copy.

Centralize tree traversal in a single recursive generator over items (recursing into section/group containers) that total_word_count and unresolved_markers both consume, dispatching on the item's kind.

Handle note text with two compiled regexes: strip marker tokens of the form [[?identifier]] first (capturing identifiers for the unresolved set), then count words as \b\w+\b runs in the stripped text; references contribute their declared word_count and their unresolved list verbatim.
Render the outline with a recursive walker that emits the workspace title, then each item as two spaces per nesting depth plus '<kind>: <title>', joining lines deterministically with newlines.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a container item), and check all failure conditions (string ids, existence, container-ness, self/descendant containment via a subtree scan, integer index within 0..len(destination)) before any mutation, guaranteeing failed moves leave the data untouched; on success pop from the source list and insert/append into the destination list, carrying the item's whole subtree by reference.
mechanisms: deep-copy isolation at construction and export (copy.deepcopy)
recursive generator traversal shared by aggregation queries
kind-based dispatch for note vs. reference contribution
compiled regex pair: marker extraction/stripping then word tokenization
depth-tracked recursive outline renderer with fixed two-space indentation
validate-then-mutate move protocol for atomicity on failure
parent-list/index lookup helper and subtree containment check to reject cyclic moves
